facts.fact: The Home Affairs digital ID plan has recently reached a trial of the MyMzanzi app, and the digital ID has been publicly trialled, according to the Business Day opinion piece by Research ICT Africa's Drew Haller.

ZAF.note: The document says nothing on links between the civil register and the ID system.
The Information Regulator is named only in a call for independent oversight of biometrics, with no statement of its appointment or rulings.

facts.fact: A privacy impact assessment in compliance with the Protection of Personal Information Act is a legal precondition to gazetting the digital ID amendment regulations, per Research ICT Africa's submission as reported.
Amendments to the South Africa Identification Act were proposed in June 2026, so the Act exists and is being amended for digital ID; the article reports Research ICT Africa's submission on them.

ZAF.note: Digital cover is not stated: the amendment regulations are not yet gazetted.
Only about 4 million undocumented people and 341,000 unclaimed Smart IDs are given, with no share of the population holding an ID.
The document says nothing on an ID number at birth.
The document does not say who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the ID number is described.

facts.fact: The Smart ID has been issued since its launch in 2013, with 341,000 issued cards unclaimed as Home Affairs urges collection before the 4 November 2026 elections, the opinion piece says.

ZAF.note: The document says nothing on local government office connections.

facts.fact: Research ICT Africa submitted a response on the proposed Identification Act amendments, naming missing preconditions such as a digital identity policy and a privacy impact assessment, and is running a digital ID study in the Western Cape, Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal.

Proposed amendments to the South Africa Identification Act were released in June 2026 and drew multistakeholder feedback, including a Research ICT Africa submission; the article says the participatory review is still under way.
